title: The PM2.5 employment proxy does not recover the heat-work-loss signal
subtitle: Across 21 aligned year-and-parameter tests, top-three overlap with Lancet heat-loss never exceeds one economy.
finding: Across 21 aligned year-and-parameter tests, the WDI PM2.5 × employment proxy shares at most one of its top three economies with the Lancet Countdown heat-related potential work-hours-loss measure. Sixteen tests have zero overlap; five have one.
finding_short: Maximum top-three overlap with heat loss is 1 of 3 economies.
limits: Potential hours are modelled capacity losses, not observed absence from work.
Heat and PM2.5 remain separate pathways; the result does not rank economy performance.
The inherited total-population worker calculation inflated outdoor-worker denominators by up to 5×.
key_messages: The proxy’s top three never match the heat top three in 2018–2020 annual tests.
Sixteen of twenty-one specification tests show zero top-three overlap.
Retire the old workday-loss-pressure ranking; keep PM2.5 and heat separate.

sections.title: An inherited ranking that needed a construct test
sections.body: An inherited regional screen multiplied national PM2.5 exposure by an agriculture-plus-industry employment share and presented the resulting order as workday-loss pressure. That is only defensible if the proxy recovers a heat-work-loss signal.

sections.title: External validation fails
sections.body: Across three aligned years, seven proxy specifications, and 21 tests, maximum top-three overlap with Lancet heat loss is one economy. In 2020 the proxy top three are India, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh; the heat top three are Cambodia, Myanmar, and Thailand.

sections.title: What was compared
sections.body: The proxy uses WDI PM2.5 and employment shares. The heat measure is Lancet Countdown potential work hours lost. Tests are pre-specified year and parameter alignments, not a search for a flattering specification.

sections.title: Denominator correction
sections.body: The inherited total-population worker calculation is 5.09 times the Lancet outdoor-worker estimate for Afghanistan, 2.72 for India, and 2.61 for Bangladesh. Employed people aged 15+ bring those ratios near one.

sections.title: Decision
sections.body: Retire the old workday-loss-pressure ranking. Publish the negative external-validation result. Keep PM2.5 and heat as separate pathways.

non_claim: Potential hours are modelled capacity losses, not observed absence. The result is a construct-validation finding, not an economy ranking.
